summary.headline: Tata Chemicals Q4 FY26 consolidated EBITDA fell to INR 274 crores from INR 327 crores, with a INR 1,837 crore goodwill impairment in US.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue fell 2% YoY to INR 3,438 crores in Q4 FY26, with EBITDA at INR 274 crores versus INR 327 crores a year earlier on subdued soda ash prices across geographies. An exceptional charge of INR 1,837 crores for US goodwill impairment (USD 208 million) and a INR 159 crores deferred tax write-off drove a loss after exceptional items. Standalone revenue rose 3% to INR 1,254 crores but EBITDA fell 6% to INR 216 crores on lower realisation. Management said the West Asia conflict raised input and shipping costs, which were largely passed through, and that the company exited unremunerative Southeast Asia exports.

segments.name: India soda ash (Gujarat, Mithapur)
segments.commentary: Produced 1 million tons of soda ash in the year, higher than last year; price drop was offset by volume, but EBITDA fell on higher fixed costs.

segments.name: US (soda ash)
segments.commentary: Lower exports and unremunerative Southeast Asia realisations; EBITDA improved sequentially as the company stopped selling into loss-making markets. Goodwill impaired by USD 208 million.

segments.name: UK
segments.commentary: Revenue fell on lower volumes, partly offset by price. EBITDA turned negative as a planned April shutdown was preponed into March; management says the shutdown will improve future operating parameters.

segments.name: Kenya
segments.commentary: Volumes rose and partly offset lower realisation. 50 kilo tons electric calciner soda ash operationalised; HFO supply cover is about 40-45 days and alternate sources are being secured.

segments.name: Singapore (Novabay Pte Ltd)
segments.commentary: Acquisition completed on 19 March 2026, during the quarter.

segments.name: Rallis
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 6%, volume 5% and price 1%, driven by crop care and seeds.

guidance_outlook: Management says it is fully covered on input costs in India, US and UK on a weighted-average basis; Q4 margins are expected to reflect current conditions, but it will update if costs move materially.
FY27 capex of about INR 1,300 crores, mainly maintenance capex at Mithapur and US plus growth capex at Valinokkam, Silica and Singapore; net debt expected to stay at roughly the March 2026 level.
Immediate debottlenecking capacity expansion of INR 100 crores expected on stream in 12 to 14 months, with returns above 20%.
No US soda ash capex until the cycle turns; investment focus is on non-soda ash businesses such as bicarbonate, salt, bromine and chemicals.

Management expects margin and profitability improvements over the next few quarters from exiting unremunerative exports and focusing on domestic sales; more detail on post-conflict effects promised for the Q1 FY27 call.
capex_capacity: Cuddalore precipitated silica plant (about 50,000 tons, INR 775 crores incremental capex) is under detailed review; expected returns 15-20%. Management did not disclose revenue or EBITDA.

Valinokkam dense ash plant is a repurposing of an existing cement plant, with returns of about 20%; it is expected to serve solar glass demand of about 7,500-10,000 tons a month at initial ramp-up, with at least 50% utilisation expected.
Valinokkam salt plant is expected to earn about 20%, with freight savings in southern markets offsetting higher capital intensity versus Mithapur.
Sodium bicarbonate output in India rose from about 140,000 tons to 290,000 tons and is fully sold out, with NTPC as the largest buyer.
Mining rights in India remain intact; they are amortised over about 100 years.
demand_pricing: Imports into India fell to about half of the pre-conflict level of 70,000-100,000 tons a month, as Iranian and Turkish exports slowed. Customers are shifting toward domestic supply, and importers are requesting higher allocations.

China spot export offers held at USD 150-170; Chinese inventories are about 1.8 million tons and stable; Chinese prices are flat at about 1,250 renminbi per ton. Management expects pricing to stay range-bound, with some producers passing on energy costs.
A US producer with 1.36 million tons of capacity has mothballed its plant, and Solvay cut about 180,000 tons of production in Spain. Management says most closures were initiated before the conflict.
Kenya gas-linked costs rose about 50-60% in the market once cover runs out. Management says this is an availability issue, and pass-through is under way.

Government may impose safeguard duty with quantity restrictions and reinstate anti-dumping duty on soda ash imports; the outcome is pending. Ammonia supply to non-fertilizer users has been restricted, affecting about 1% of national ammonia consumption.

qa_highlights.question: How is the Middle East conflict affecting raw material sourcing across regions?
qa_highlights.answer: US is largely insulated. UK brine is self-sourced, with an unhedged gas price issue only. In India, imported coal from Indonesia is flowing and imported limestone is being blended with domestic supply, with no major issues for three months. Kenya depends on HFO from the Middle East, with about 40-45 days of cover.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q4 margin the bottom, and will customers move to mid-term contracts?
qa_highlights.answer: Management would not commit beyond current visibility, saying it is fully covered and the numbers reflect current conditions. Customers are more focused on domestic sourcing and some importers are requesting higher allocations.

qa_highlights.question: Why did US EBITDA improve sequentially, and what is the export mix?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it stopped selling into unremunerative Southeast Asia markets during the quarter. No export/domestic split was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why did UK EBITDA turn negative this quarter?
qa_highlights.answer: A planned April shutdown was brought forward to March for operational and product capability changes. Management says the impact is one-off and operating parameters should improve.

qa_highlights.question: What returns are expected on the new capex, and why is Valinokkam IRR 20% given its higher capital intensity?
qa_highlights.answer: Debottlenecking INR 100 crores is expected to return above 20%. Valinokkam is expected at about 20%, with freight savings in southern markets offsetting the higher capital cost. Silica is expected at 15-20%, based on a freight advantage in the South.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and net debt outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex is about INR 1,300 crores, mostly maintenance in Mithapur and US plus growth in South India and Singapore. Net debt is expected to stay at about the March 2026 level.

qa_highlights.question: Is the goodwill write-down linked to mining rights, and what is the Cuddalore silica project's return?
qa_highlights.answer: Only goodwill of USD 208 million was impaired; mining rights are intact and amortised over about 100 years. Cuddalore silica project details (revenue, EBITDA) were deferred to Q1 FY27 call; the INR 775 crores is all incremental capex.

risks_watch: Kenya HFO supply: about 40-45 days of cover; alternate sources are being secured, and a prolonged Middle East conflict could raise costs or disrupt supply.
Customer stress from pass-through of cost increases, and the possibility of demand erosion if the conflict continues.
Chinese inventories (about 1.8 million tons) and any shutdowns of older plants that could reduce global oversupply.
Pending Indian government decisions on anti-dumping duty, safeguard duty with quantity restrictions, and ammonia supply restrictions.
Operating cash flow decline and working capital build; management expects the cycle to improve as the mix shifts toward domestic sales.
Deferred tax asset of INR 159 crores written off; future reversal depends on the unit becoming profitable.
summary.management_tone: Candid and cautious: management acknowledged a difficult quarter and an uncertain operating environment, but was confident that input costs are fully passed through in India and the US. It was guarded on Kenya, the post-conflict demand outlook and detail on the Cuddalore silica project, deferring several questions to the Q1 FY27 call.
key_quotes: It's been a difficult quarter and a difficult operating environment, but what we are focused on is disciplined execution, strengthening the supply chain responsiveness, maintaining strict cost and cash flow discipline.
We're fully covered and as far as the numbers are concerned, they should reflect what we've seen.
We are not doing beyond what is the cost increase.
Our investments are fundamentally focused on non-soda ash businesses, which is bicarbonate, salt, bromine and various other chemicals.

rows.why: Management expects pricing to stay range-bound with some producers passing on energy costs, while a US producer with 1.36 mt capacity mothballed and Solvay cut ~180,000 tons in Spain, so the oversupply is easing only slowly.

rows.label: India safeguard / anti-dumping duty on soda ash imports pending
rows.why: Government may impose safeguard duty with quantity restrictions and reinstate anti-dumping duty, and imports have already fallen to about half of the 70,000-100,000 tons a month pre-conflict level.
